overrides.reason: The strict pre-vote HF3684 version establishes measurable grant scoring, authorizes the Veterans Affairs commissioner to withhold grant money when a grantee committed fraud or is under criminal investigation, and requires recurring grantee reporting on grant amounts, other public grants, services, outcomes, and charitable-giving ratios. Those are direct oversight and accountability controls for a state grant program and align with Allen's broad anti-fraud/accountability proposition.

The strict pre-vote HF4252 version creates a fraud-denial rule for student aid and grant programs administered under chapter 136A: funding may be denied for materially false or fraudulent applications, refusal of reasonable inspection or information requests, or a fraud/material-violation determination involving government funding. These are direct state-program anti-fraud and oversight controls and align with Allen's proposition.

The strict pre-vote SF4760 version gives the BCA superintendent subpoena authority for financial-crime and fraud investigations, expressly including fraud involving state-funded or state-administered programs or services. That is a concrete new oversight and investigative tool for state-program fraud and aligns with Allen's broad accountability proposition.

SF4760 directly amends repeat-impaired-driving license-revocation and ignition-interlock provisions and broadens parts of the program-participant definition, so it is genuinely in the same policy lane. But the exact version does not safely establish Kraft's combined proposition of materially more aggressive interlock time for repeat DWI offenders while also reducing barriers to program entry. Same-program overlap is therefore fail-closed.
